canonicalOnly.reason: The keys convention: a tracker row that makes a door-closing claim carries a Check that turns it. Canonical-only because the keys are, and a README for files the beta does not hold would describe nothing there.

Turns DATA-GAP-REGISTER TSPY-11's "a reaches_caster filter is not the fix". Reads contract/*/powersets, which the beta does not carry in this layout, and mirrors a Rust predicate (reaches_caster) the beta's TS engine spells differently — so a beta copy would grade a different question under the same name. The register naming it is a docs/ reference, outside verify-sync's WIRING_PATHS, and the same already-stated condition as the docs/gaps/ narratives its rows cite (lint-register-shape.cjs rule 6).

Turns the Kheldian shapeshift residual's "nothing is granted through this channel". Walks exported_powers/, the 746 MB export tree, which is canonical-only. Same docs/-reference reasoning as the sibling key.

Turns the REBUILD-PROGRESS `effects` writer-side row's "the reader side is done, so what is left is an emitter edit plus a regen". Reads contract/ and crates/*/src — the emitted bundle and the Rust engine, neither of which the beta carries. Its Rust leg is the point: the beta has no crates/ at all, so a mirrored copy would silently report zero raw-`effects` readers and read as a green light to strip. Same docs/-reference reasoning as the sibling keys.

Turns DATA-GAP-REGISTER FORK-4's "keep sync:shared off the shared test surface". Reads BOTH repos' whole git history for each shared test path, so it can only run where the private canonical tree is the cwd and the beta is the sibling — the beta cannot see canonical at all, and a copy there would grade one repo against itself and always find the surface one-way. That is the failure mode the key exists to prevent, so a mirrored copy would be worse than none. Same docs/-reference reasoning as the sibling keys.

MBDEXPORT-8's measurement: how many names differ from Mids' only in their separators. Canonical-only for the reason every key is — it reads `exported_powers/` and `tools/mids-oracle/`, neither of which the beta holds, and it shells out to `convert-mids-name-map.cjs --pairs` for the powerset pairing rather than re-deriving it. Its answer (1 across four datasets, 0 ambiguous) is what let the join be widened for the writer alone; re-run it after an HC rename sweep.

MBDEXPORT-9's roster: every powerset the three pairing passes leave unpaired, each with the reason it is unreachable rather than merely unreached. Canonical-only for the reason every key is — it reads exported_powers/ and tools/mids-oracle/, neither of which the beta holds, and it shells out to convert-mids-name-map.cjs --pairs for the pairing rather than re-deriving it. It reds (exit 1) on a set of ours whose exact roster is held by one unpaired Mids set, which is pass three's own population; re-run it after a fork rename sweep or a Mids database bump.

Wired into canonical's regen-all.cjs and package.json as audit:census. Same shape as the twins ratchet: an unreferenced beta copy whose --gate leg reads scripts/audit-census-baseline.json, absent there.

Wired into canonical's regen-all.cjs and package.json as audit:override-staleness. Cross-fork by construction: it grades every dataset's override layer against that dataset's own generated twin, and the beta carries neither the four-dataset tree nor the generated layer to compare.

Canonical-only converter for the archetype inherents tree, wired into regen-all.cjs. The beta has never carried the file, so the manifest's present-in-both check never fired on it and its absence was undeclared rather than adjudicated — found while routing every display_help emitter through helpText. Both names of it in the beta are prose in comments (the convert-side twin, the family it omits), not a require.

Reads fixtures/mids/, the corpus of Mids-written .mbd files, which lives in canonical because that is where the Rust reader will grade against it — the beta has no fixtures/ tree at all. Both copies of the importer were run against the corpus on 2026-09-09 and returned identical summaries, so this gate's verdict covers the beta's copy; the day they diverge, that is what the pinned counts here will say.

Reads fixtures/mids/, which lives in canonical alone — the beta has no fixtures/ tree. It grades the seam rather than either half: a corpus file is read, written back out, and the OUTPUT is checked against Mids' own vocabulary, which is what MBDEXPORT-4 needed and no in-process round trip could give. Its verdict covers the beta's writer too: the beta's mids-export.ts is a declared SLOT-3 fork, and the same MBDEXPORT-4 edit was applied to it by hand on 2026-09-09 — that hand carry, not this gate, is what the fork row owes.

Pins what a Thunderspy build becomes as a .mbd (MBDEXPORT-2). Reads fixtures/skif/v4/thunderpy-primalist.skif, and the beta has no fixtures/ tree — the same reason as the .mbd corpus gate beside it. It is un-carryable for a second reason worth naming, because the first one would go away if the beta ever grew fixtures: it calls the one-arg `exportToMidsWithReport(build)`, and the beta's takes a `levelUpMode` second argument (SLOT-3), so it would not type-check there. What it grades is therefore canonical's forked copy and not the one users run. The two copies differ in three hunks, all slot levels, so every assertion here holds for the beta's copy too — this gate asserts nothing about a slot's `Level`.

Wired into beta's package.json as changelog:push and read by src/data/changelog-manual.ts; it posts the beta site's changelog to a Discord webhook, and canonical has no such entry point. Canonical kept an archived copy under scripts/attic/ and it went 100 lines stale — the beta gained id-keyed dedup and unknown-flag rejection in cc193fb3f8, canonical never had it, and the attic move had already taken the file off the path this manifest keys on.

The machine copy for the shared surface this manifest adjudicates, wired into the beta's package.json as sync:shared. Beta-only for the same reason sync-bin-crawler.sh is: it runs in the repo that RECEIVES, because it overwrites, and a canonical copy would be a script pointing the wrong way down a one-way street. It reads canonical's manifest for the file list and runs canonical's verify-sync.cjs --write, so canonical needs no copy of it to participate.

entries.reason: Two censuses of two different applications that share a name and an appendix. Canonical's is the REBUILD's inventory — every menu, popover and control row in the Dioxus app, written to answer one question (what rule decides which surface a new setting goes to), with the beta enumerated as the comparison baseline in an appendix. Beta's copy is that appendix alone. Converging them means one repo carrying an inventory of an app it is not: the 135 lines above canonical's appendix name Dioxus components beta does not have, and beta's own enumeration is the thing canonical is measuring itself AGAINST, so it cannot be dropped there either. The shared appendix text drifts in citation style only (canonical cites paths as code spans, beta as markdown links), which is a document each repo renders its own way rather than a pipeline behaviour, so nothing downstream reads either file.

The stage roster and the gate roster ARE the repo's identity — which converters exist and which gates it can currently pass — so two repos with different pipelines have different stage lists by definition. Re-measured 2026-08-29; the 2026-08-21 figures had gone stale on both halves (beta gained convert-accolades.cjs on 2026-08-22, and canonical's bag strip aaab1c4077 deleted seven post-loop blocks). Strip the comments, the STEPS body and the post-loop blocks and what is left is a 21-line driver, byte-identical, so all the divergence is in the two parts a shared table would have to hold. Canonical runs 22 stages to beta's 15 and neither is a subset: 14 shared, 8 canonical-only (convert-boost-index, convert-special-enhancements, convert-inherents, convert-incarnate-slot-indices, detect-chance-mod-selectors, detect-caster-meters, validate-converter-output, dsh8-incarnate-collapse-detector), 1 beta-only (convert-archetype-inherents.cjs, which canonical has no copy of). Post-loop — counting each top-level if/block/for after the dataset loop that runs a command, which is the measure the 2026-08-21 note left unstated — canonical runs 16 blocks to beta's 8, and the strip made that divergence sharper rather than smaller: canonical's are 13 audit gates plus 3 emitter/fixture blocks, while beta's are dsh6 plus the seven planb-shadow gates canonical deleted along with the bag they read. Those blocks are not a stage list: they carry dataset predicates, existsSync optionality, a python3 runner, a ts-esm-register runner and two --dataset arg conventions, so a declarative table for them is a predicate/runner/optionality DSL written to describe a list of shell commands. And a shared table is a file canonical edits and beta EXECUTES at the head of the pipeline that produces beta's committed data, where a stage carrying the wrong repo-membership flag is silent on beta's side.

Joined 2026-09-10 under FORK-7 and still differs, but no longer on the thing that mattered: `isInherentlyAttuned` is now one shared block in both copies, reading the export's `attunedOnly` instead of the hand list of set names the two repos had disagreed about since 2026-07-30 (MBDEXPORT-14). What remains is older drift the 80e28b2b6a transplant left — the beta imports `genericIOValueAtLevel` where canonical imports `getAspectSchedule`/`getIOValueAtLevel`, four slotting-category headings sit in a different order behind the same set, and several comments are reflowed. Neither copy is the older form of the other; both sides authored.

Declares the Shared Builds social feature's Supabase row shape (SharedBuild, ShareBuildInput, SearchFilters). It sits in src/types/ next to the genuinely-shared game-data types but nothing in canonical's converters or Rust crates reads it -- it rode into the manifest as 'identical' on the wholesale src/ transplant, not on a require edge (FORK-5). Canonical's copy is frozen by design (README: edited only by regen, which never touches it); beta's is the live feature type, evolving with the deployed Shared Builds feature (this visibility rework: private/unlisted/public replacing the is_public boolean).

SLOT-3 (beta commit d59d7d3d5c): beta's `exportToMids` / `exportToMidsWithReport` take a second `levelUpMode` parameter and resolve slot levels through `computeExportSlotLevels`, so off-mode placement stops enforcing a pick-level schedule floor and says once in the UI that the Level it writes is synthetic. Canonical's copy keeps the one-arg form and `computeAllSlotLevels`. Three hunks, all slot levels — name rotation, enhancement UID mapping and warning emission are byte-identical, so every MBDEXPORT pin taken against canonical's copy holds for the beta's except a claim about a slot's `Level`. Canonical's copy is not app code: it is the source the Rust `.mbd` writer will be ported from, and `crates/app/src/build_io.rs` still lists `.mbd`/`.mxd` as not in the rebuild. Port THIS copy and Rust inherits the floor SLOT-3 removed, stamping every exported slot with a levelling history the build never had — a Rule 1 soft-wrong value written into a file another planner reads as authoritative. CARRIED 2026-09-10, and the sentence above is why it had to be: MBDEXPORT-13 changed `StatInclude` in canonical's copy on 2026-09-10 and that is not a slot-level hunk, so "every MBDEXPORT pin holds for the beta's copy except a claim about a slot's `Level`" was false for a day while `verify:sync` read as ordinary stamp lag. The beta ships this writer to users (`ExportImportModal.tsx`), so the cost was a real one: a power the author excluded came back included. The `isActive === true` hunk was hand-ported to the beta and the fork is slot-levels-only again. A correctness fix crossing this fork is a hand port by construction — `sync:shared` skips a declared fork — so the claim is maintained, not automatic.
entries.exit: canonical's vendored TS half takes SLOT-3 through all ten `slot-levels.ts` consumers (Header, PowerRow, useSlotLevels, useBuildBudget, uiStore, buildStore, export-print, forum-export, mids-export, mids-import/importer), or that half is retired once the Rust writer lands. Not a carry either way: `--write` cannot converge a fork and `sync:shared` refuses to clobber a beta-authored edit, so this side will not converge on its own. Whichever comes first, the Rust `.mbd` writer must be ported from the BETA's two-arg form, and this row is where that is recorded.

entries.reason: SLOT-3: beta's import call now passes ensureSlotOrderPopulated a live levelUpMode flag (false here — this pure parser has no store access, so the store's own importMidsBuild action re-runs the call against the real mode right after) so off-mode slot placement stops enforcing a pick-level schedule floor. Canonical's copy still calls the one-arg form; canonical's slot-levels.ts has no levelUpMode parameter to receive it. MBDIMPORT-8 (2026-09-10) widened the fork: canonical derives the imported character level from Mids' GetMaxLevel floor raised by the leveling schedule (src/utils/mids-import/character-level.ts, canonical-only), where beta still carries the maxPowerEntryLevel >= 49 ? 50 heuristic. MBDIMPORT-11 (2026-09-10) widened it again on the same seam: canonical now warns when a file places more budget slots than the server's schedule grants at any level, which only the character-level derivation can measure, so beta has no half of it to fork. CARRIED 2026-09-10, same episode as `src/utils/mids-export.ts`: MBDEXPORT-13's reader halves (the include flag on an inherent entry, and the form sub-power `isActive` override) and MBDEXPORT-15's (an all-empty inherent entry dropped whole, losing the placements the file is the only record of) were canonical-only for a day and rode inside this fork undeclared. All three were hand-ported to the beta, which ships this reader to users. What remains is SLOT-3, MBDIMPORT-8 and MBDIMPORT-11 — the three this reason already names, and nothing else.
entries.exit: canonical's own TS import tooling adopts the same levelUpMode-aware call (or a maintainer confirms it doesn't need SLOT-3's fix), then a --write carries the converged hash across. sync:shared only flows canonical to beta and refuses to clobber a beta-authored edit, so this side won't converge on its own. Re-cut 2026-09-09 with its two source twins: the first half of that will not happen on its own — canonical's `src/` is not tooling that adopts things, it is the tree the Rust port reads — so the condition that actually binds is that the Rust `.mbd` READER be ported from the beta's levelUpMode-aware call, the same way the writer must be (see `src/utils/mids-export.ts`).

entries.reason: SLOT-3 (beta commit d59d7d3d5c), and the module the `mids-export.ts` fork beside it actually lives in: 690 lines to the beta's 879. `computeAllSlotLevels`, `ensureSlotOrderPopulated`, `backfillSlotOrderLevels`, `canMoveSlotLevel` and `applySlotLevelMove` all gained a trailing `levelUpMode`, and the beta added `computeExportSlotLevels`, `reconcileStoredSlotLevels` and `scrubFabricatedSlotLevels`, which canonical has no counterpart for.
